findings.title: Foundation parameters are selected by ambiguous localized names
findings.body: LookupParameter("Length") and LookupParameter("Width") depend on the displayed parameter name and return an arbitrary match when multiple parameters share that name. Consequently, localized Revit installations or families with same-named project/shared parameters can reject an otherwise valid family or write dimensions into the wrong parameters. The same unsafe lookup is repeated while matching and modifying types. Resolve dimensions through stable built-in/Forge parameter identifiers or an explicitly configured shared-parameter GUID, and validate storage type before reading or setting values.

findings.title: Foundations can be assigned to an arbitrary level
findings.body: When the active view has no GenLevel, which is normal for a 3D view, the command uses FirstElement() from an unordered collector. This level is not derived from the CAD outline elevation and is not guaranteed to be the nearest or intended foundation level. The resulting elements can therefore have an incorrect Level association and offset even though their XY geometry was parsed correctly. Select the level deterministically from the outline elevation or require the user to choose one, and fail explicitly if no level exists.

findings.title: Non-planar CAD loops are flattened into foundations
findings.body: ProcessPoints calculates minZ and maxZ but never uses them to enforce planarity. It only checks the Z component of the longest edge, so a tilted rectangle whose longest sides are horizontal and whose shorter sides vary in Z passes validation. Projection then discards the vertical component, shortens the computed width, and places a horizontal foundation at the first vertex's elevation. Reject loops whose Z range exceeds tolerance, or project onto and validate an explicitly supported CAD plane.

findings.title: Greedy line chaining loses valid outlines at shared vertices
findings.body: BuildLoops consumes the first line touching the current endpoint without backtracking or graph-based cycle detection. Duplicate lines, coincident outlines, or two foundation rectangles sharing a corner introduce multiple candidate edges; iteration order can then make the algorithm follow the wrong branch and permanently remove lines from consideration. The malformed chain is discarded and valid foundations are silently omitted. Construct an endpoint graph and extract closed cycles deterministically while preserving unused edges.
